purpose: This instruction file defines how the coding agent should build, extend, and refactor the Flutter/Firebase app while preserving the existing architecture, consistency, and maintainability.
primaryMission: Implement features by following the existing repository structure instead of inventing a new pattern.
Keep the app modular, scalable, and easy to maintain.
Ensure UI, business logic, data access, and state management remain clearly separated.
corePrinciples: Do not mix UI code and business logic in the same file.
Always place screen/view code in presentation-layer files and move logic to dedicated application, domain, or data-layer files.
Keep the codebase clean, predictable, and consistent with the planned feature-first structure.
Prefer small, focused changes over large rewrites.
Respect the existing folder structure and only add code inside the appropriate dedicated folders.

architectureRules.featureFirstStructure: Use the existing feature-first architecture under lib/features. Each feature should be organized around its own responsibility and should not spill into unrelated modules.

uiAndLogicSeparation.rule: Never place business logic, state management, API calls, validation, repository access, or navigation decisions directly inside a screen/widget file unless the file is explicitly a controller or view-model.
uiAndLogicSeparation.uiFiles: Use files such as screens, widgets, and presentation components for rendering only.
uiAndLogicSeparation.logicFiles: Use files such as controllers, providers, services, repositories, use cases, models, and state classes for logic and data flow.
uiAndLogicSeparation.widgetRule: If a screen needs a reusable widget, create a dedicated widget file in the relevant widget folder or shared widget folder rather than embedding the widget directly inside the screen file.

folderGuidance.widgets: lib/features/<feature>/presentation/widgets for feature-specific widgets or lib/shared/widgets for reusable app-wide widgets
folderGuidance.controllers: lib/features/<feature>/presentation/controllers when a dedicated controller is needed
folderGuidance.state: lib/features/<feature>/presentation/providers for feature state and UI state management
folderGuidance.services: lib/core/services for shared app services; place feature-specific data access under lib/features/<feature>/data/datasources
folderGuidance.models: lib/features/<feature>/data/models for data models and lib/features/<feature>/domain/entities for domain entities
folderGuidance.routing: lib/router.dart for app-wide navigation and feature-specific navigation helpers only when necessary
folderGuidance.providers: lib/features/<feature>/presentation/providers for feature providers and lib/core/providers for shared app-level providers

constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedColors: Do not hardcode colors directly inside widgets, screens, or logic files. Use lib/core/theme/app_colors.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedFonts: Do not hardcode font styles directly in UI code. Use lib/core/theme/app_fonts.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedIcons: Do not use raw icon literals without centralizing them. Use lib/core/constants/app_icons.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedStrings: Do not hardcode user-visible strings inside widgets or screens. Use lib/core/localization/app_strings.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedSizes: Do not hardcode dimensions, padding, margins, icon sizes, or component sizes. Use lib/core/constants/app_sizes.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedSpacing: Do not hardcode spacing values. Use lib/core/theme/app_spacing.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedAssets: Do not reference images, illustrations, or asset paths directly in code. Use lib/core/constants/app_assets.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.noHardcodedRadius: Do not hardcode border radius values. Use lib/core/theme/app_radius.dart.
constantsAndStyleRules.createMissingConstants: If a required token does not exist yet, create it in the appropriate central file rather than injecting a raw value locally.

agentWorkflow.step1: Read the relevant planning files first: Plans/BCS_Booster_AI_Agent_Prompt.md, Plans/BCS_Booster_AI_Agent_Implementation_Steps.md, Plans/design.md, Plans/widgetdesign.md, and Plans/appflow.md.
agentWorkflow.step2: Inspect the existing codebase structure and find the closest feature, screen, widget, provider, or service that matches the requested implementation.
agentWorkflow.step3: Understand the current architecture pattern before editing anything. Reuse existing providers, services, route setup, and UI conventions.
agentWorkflow.step4: Split the task into UI work and logic work. Create or update presentation files for rendering and dedicated logic files for behavior and state.
agentWorkflow.step5: Place new reusable widgets in the correct widget folder and keep screen files focused on composition and layout.
agentWorkflow.step6: Centralize all style values and strings in the designated constants files.
agentWorkflow.step7: Make changes scoped to the feature or shared layer that owns the responsibility. Do not modify unrelated modules unless required for integration.
agentWorkflow.step8: Verify the implementation by checking for compile issues, missing imports, and consistency with the project pattern.

implementationGuidelines: Always inspect similar existing features before creating a new one.
Prefer small, composable widgets over large monolithic screen files.
If a widget is only used by one screen, keep it near that screen unless it is clearly reusable across the app.
Use existing routing, dependency injection, and state-management patterns rather than introducing new ones unless the project already expects them.
Maintain naming consistency with the rest of the project.
Write code that is readable, testable, and easy for another agent to extend later.
Avoid magic numbers, inline styles, and duplicated UI fragments.

qualityExpectations.maintainability: Code should be easy to follow and should clearly separate responsibilities.
qualityExpectations.consistency: UI should look and behave consistently with the design guide and existing app standards.
qualityExpectations.scalability: The implementation should support future expansion without turning into a tightly coupled file.
qualityExpectations.safety: Avoid introducing runtime errors, missing imports, or broken navigation flows.

forbiddenPatterns: Do not place API calls inside a widget file.
Do not place controller logic inside the screen UI file.
Do not hardcode colors, strings, images, dimensions, spacing, border radius, or icons.
Do not create a giant screen file containing both layout and business logic.
Do not add ad-hoc widgets directly inside a screen file when a dedicated widget file is appropriate.
Do not create new folders randomly; use the existing project structure.
Do not ignore existing providers, services, or router patterns.
Do not implement features without checking how similar features are structured.
bestPracticesForBestOutput: Start by understanding the requirement deeply before coding.
Read the related files, not just the target file.
Follow the existing naming conventions and architecture language used by the project.
Keep code modular and focused on one responsibility per file.
Make the implementation production-friendly, not just functional.
Leave the codebase easier to maintain than you found it.
Document important architectural decisions only if the project already uses documentation for that purpose.
agentBehaviorRules: If unsure, inspect similar code before changing anything.
When implementing a screen, create or update the UI file, the widget files, and the logic/state files separately.
When implementing a feature, wire it through the correct layer instead of bypassing the architecture.
When the request is large, break it into smaller, verifiable steps.
Before finishing, review the diff for accidental mixing of UI and logic or inconsistent hardcoded values.
finalDeliverableStandard: The agent should produce code that is organized, clean, modular, architecture-aligned, and ready for integration into the existing Flutter/Firebase project.
